pillars.name: Technology Infrastructure
pillars.description: Evaluate your organization's technical foundation and capabilities for AI implementation.

questions.text: How would you rate your organization's current data infrastructure?
questions.description: Consider data storage, accessibility, quality, and integration capabilities.
questions.weight_rationale: Data infrastructure is fundamental to any AI initiative

meanings.1: Data is stored in silos with no integration or standardization
meanings.2: Some centralized storage but limited integration and data quality issues
meanings.3: Centralized systems with some integration and data governance practices
meanings.4: Well-integrated systems with strong data governance and quality processes
meanings.5: Modern, cloud-native architecture with real-time integration and advanced analytics capabilities

questions.text: What is your organization's cloud computing maturity?
questions.description: Assess your cloud adoption, scalability, and modern architecture practices.
questions.weight_rationale: Cloud infrastructure provides the scalability and flexibility needed for AI workloads

meanings.1: Entirely on-premises infrastructure with no cloud services
meanings.2: Limited use of basic cloud services for storage or backup
meanings.3: Some applications moved to cloud with hybrid architecture
meanings.4: Most systems cloud-based with good DevOps practices
meanings.5: Fully cloud-native with microservices, containers, and automated scaling

questions.text: How mature are your API and integration capabilities?
questions.description: Consider system interoperability, API management, and real-time data exchange.
questions.weight_rationale: APIs are essential for AI system integration and data flow

meanings.1: Systems operate in isolation with manual data transfer
meanings.2: Simple integrations between key systems using basic methods
meanings.3: Some RESTful APIs developed with basic management practices
meanings.4: Well-designed API strategy with governance, security, and monitoring
meanings.5: Sophisticated API ecosystem with GraphQL, event-driven architecture, and comprehensive management

pillars.name: Data Management
pillars.description: Assess your organization's data governance, quality, and analytics capabilities.

questions.text: How would you describe your data governance practices?
questions.description: Consider data policies, ownership, privacy compliance, and quality standards.
questions.weight_rationale: Strong data governance is critical for AI ethics and compliance

meanings.1: No formal policies, unclear data ownership, limited compliance measures
meanings.2: Basic policies exist but inconsistent enforcement and limited privacy controls
meanings.3: Structured governance framework with defined roles and some compliance processes
meanings.4: Comprehensive policies with clear ownership, strong privacy controls, and regular auditing
meanings.5: Industry-leading governance with automated compliance, advanced privacy protection, and proactive risk management

questions.text: What is the overall quality and consistency of your organizational data?
questions.description: Evaluate data accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and standardization.
questions.weight_rationale: High-quality data is essential for reliable AI model performance

meanings.1: Significant issues with accuracy, completeness, and consistency across systems
meanings.2: Data quality varies significantly between systems with manual correction processes
meanings.3: Generally good quality with some standardization and periodic quality checks
meanings.4: High-quality data with automated validation, standardization, and regular monitoring
meanings.5: Superior data quality with real-time validation, comprehensive lineage tracking, and proactive quality management

questions.text: How advanced are your current analytics and reporting capabilities?
questions.description: Consider business intelligence, self-service analytics, and predictive capabilities.
questions.weight_rationale: Analytics maturity indicates readiness for more advanced AI applications

meanings.1: Manual reporting with basic charts and tables from spreadsheets or simple tools
meanings.2: Standard BI tools with dashboards and structured reports but limited self-service capability
meanings.3: Self-service analytics with data visualization and some statistical analysis capabilities
meanings.4: Predictive models in production with machine learning-based forecasting and optimization
meanings.5: Sophisticated AI-powered analytics with automated insights, natural language querying, and advanced machine learning

pillars.name: Organizational Culture
pillars.description: Evaluate your organization's cultural readiness for AI adoption and digital transformation.

questions.text: How receptive is your organization to technological change and innovation?
questions.description: Consider leadership support, employee attitudes, and change management capabilities.
questions.weight_rationale: Cultural acceptance is crucial for successful AI implementation and adoption

meanings.1: Strong resistance to new technologies with preference for traditional methods
meanings.2: Skeptical of new technology with slow adoption and limited leadership support
meanings.3: Open to change with proper justification and gradual implementation approach
meanings.4: Actively seeks technological improvements with strong leadership support for innovation
meanings.5: Innovation is core to organizational identity with rapid adoption of emerging technologies

questions.text: What is your organization's current level of digital skills and AI literacy?
questions.description: Assess technical capabilities, training programs, and learning culture.
questions.weight_rationale: Employee skills and literacy directly impact AI implementation success

responses.5: Advanced AI and data science skills

meanings.1: Most employees have basic computer skills with limited technical training programs
meanings.2: Employees comfortable with standard software but limited technical or analytical skills
meanings.3: Some technical specialists with moderate analytical capabilities and ongoing training
meanings.4: Strong technical skills across organization with data literacy and continuous learning
meanings.5: Deep technical expertise with AI/ML specialists and comprehensive upskilling programs

questions.text: How effectively do different departments collaborate on technology initiatives?
questions.description: Consider cross-functional teamwork, communication, and shared objectives.
questions.weight_rationale: AI initiatives require strong cross-functional collaboration

meanings.1: Departments work independently with minimal communication or shared goals
meanings.2: Some collaboration on major projects but generally separate planning and execution
meanings.3: Regular cross-functional projects with defined processes for collaboration
meanings.4: Strong culture of teamwork with shared metrics and integrated planning processes
meanings.5: Fluid organizational boundaries with agile, cross-functional teams as the standard operating model

pillars.name: Strategic Planning
pillars.description: Assess your organization's strategic approach to AI adoption and digital transformation.

questions.text: How well-defined is your organization's AI strategy and vision?
questions.description: Consider strategic clarity, executive commitment, and roadmap development.
questions.weight_rationale: Clear AI strategy is fundamental to successful implementation and ROI

meanings.1: No formal discussion or planning around AI adoption
meanings.2: Ad-hoc conversations about AI potential but no formal planning process
meanings.3: Strategy development in progress with some executive engagement and initial planning
meanings.4: Clear AI strategy with defined objectives, timeline, and resource allocation
meanings.5: Comprehensive transformation plan with detailed roadmap, governance, and change management

questions.text: What is your organization's approach to AI-related investments?
questions.description: Consider budget allocation, ROI expectations, and long-term commitment.
questions.weight_rationale: Investment commitment indicates serious strategic intent

meanings.1: No formal budget allocation for AI initiatives or technology
meanings.2: Small experimental budget for pilot projects or proof-of-concepts
meanings.3: Dedicated budget for AI projects with clear approval processes
meanings.4: Substantial investment in AI technology, talent, and infrastructure
meanings.5: AI is a strategic investment priority with significant multi-year financial commitment

questions.text: How mature is your governance structure for AI and data initiatives?
questions.description: Evaluate decision-making processes, oversight committees, and accountability frameworks.
questions.weight_rationale: Strong governance ensures responsible AI development and deployment

meanings.1: No formal processes for AI project approval or oversight
meanings.2: Basic approval processes with limited oversight and accountability
meanings.3: Structured committees with defined roles and decision-making processes
meanings.4: Comprehensive governance with ethics oversight, risk management, and performance monitoring
meanings.5: Industry-leading governance with automated oversight, continuous monitoring, and adaptive frameworks

pillars.name: Risk Management
pillars.description: Evaluate your organization's approach to AI-related risks, security, and compliance.

questions.text: How robust are your cybersecurity and data protection measures?
questions.description: Consider security frameworks, threat detection, and incident response capabilities.
questions.weight_rationale: Security is critical for AI systems handling sensitive data

meanings.1: Basic password policies and antivirus with limited monitoring or incident response
meanings.2: Standard security tools and policies but limited advanced threat protection
meanings.3: Comprehensive security framework with monitoring, training, and response procedures
meanings.4: Advanced security with threat intelligence, automated response, and regular security assessments
meanings.5: Sophisticated security program with AI-powered threat detection, zero-trust architecture, and continuous monitoring

questions.text: How well does your organization manage regulatory compliance and ethical considerations?
questions.description: Assess compliance frameworks, ethical guidelines, and regulatory readiness.
questions.weight_rationale: Compliance and ethics are increasingly important for AI deployment

meanings.1: Reactive approach to compliance with limited formal processes or training
meanings.2: Basic compliance programs covering key regulations but limited AI-specific considerations
meanings.3: Structured approach with dedicated compliance team and regular assessments
meanings.4: Comprehensive compliance management with AI ethics guidelines and proactive monitoring
meanings.5: Industry-leading compliance program with automated monitoring, ethical AI frameworks, and regulatory engagement

questions.text: How prepared is your organization for AI-related operational risks?
questions.description: Consider backup systems, failure recovery, and business continuity planning.
questions.weight_rationale: Business continuity planning is essential for AI-dependent operations

meanings.1: Minimal backup systems with limited disaster recovery or business continuity planning
meanings.2: Basic backup and recovery procedures but limited testing or AI-specific considerations
meanings.3: Structured risk management with business continuity plans and regular testing
meanings.4: Comprehensive planning with redundant systems, automated failover, and detailed recovery procedures
meanings.5: Advanced resilience framework with real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance, and adaptive response systems
